# Top 5 AI notetakers for decision capture

Source: https://lowob.com/research/top-5-ai-notetakers-for-decision-capture/
Publisher: lowob (https://lowob.com)
Published: 2026-10-21 · Updated: 2026-11-16
Function: Strategy

> Summary: Every notetaker now transcribes well. The difference is what happens next: whether it helps you pull out what was decided and why, whether you own and can export the record, and whether everyone on the call knew they were being recorded. Granola ranks first because it drafts notes you correct, deletes audio after transcription and exposes notes through MCP on every plan. Fireflies.ai, Fathom, Circleback and Google Meet with Gemini notes follow.

## Key points

- This list is for founders and small teams who make decisions in meetings and lose the reasons afterwards. If your firm already licenses Copilot or Gemini and every call is on one platform, start with what you have.
- Granola is $14 per user a month on Business and $35 on Enterprise, as listed in November 2026, and says audio is deleted after transcription on every plan.
- California's Penal Code section 632 makes recording a confidential communication without the consent of all parties an offence, with fines of up to $2,500 per violation.
- A proposed class action filed in August 2025 alleges Otter.ai joined meetings and recorded participants without their consent, which is why it is left off this list.
- The transcript is evidence. The decision record is what you use next month.

A notetaker is the capture end of what our explainer on [conversation intelligence](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-conversation-intelligence/) describes: software that records, transcribes and summarises calls. For decision capture the summary is not the point. What matters is getting three things out of the call and into a [decision record](https://lowob.com/research/what-is-a-decision-record/) the same day: what was decided, why, and what would change your mind. **lowob**'s piece on [the reason nobody types](https://lowob.com/research/the-reason-nobody-types/) explains why the reason is the field that goes missing.

## How we ranked

| Criterion | Weight | Why it matters |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Decision and action extraction | 30% | A transcript is evidence; a decision record is what you use next month. |
| Ownership and export | 25% | Your meeting history should not be trapped in a vendor. |
| Consent and security | 25% | Recording without clear consent is now a legal risk, not just a manners question. |
| Price for a small team | 20% | Most useful features sit behind the first paid tier. |

Consent carries a quarter of the weight for a legal reason. Several US states, including California, require the consent of every party to record a confidential conversation. California's section 632 applies to anyone who records "without the consent of all parties to a confidential communication", with fines of up to $2,500 per violation for a first offence. A notetaker that joins a call without everyone knowing is a liability for the person who invited it, whatever the vendor's terms say. This is not legal advice; check the rules where your participants are.

## The list

**1. Granola**

**Best for:** founders who want notes they edit, without a bot joining the call.

**Why it ranks first:** it runs on your laptop or phone and uses the device's audio, then drafts notes from what you jotted during the meeting. In Granola's words, "Your notes stay in black. AI additions appear in gray." That draft-and-correct pattern keeps capture fast and keeps a person responsible for what the record says, which is the property a decision record needs. Granola says "audio is deleted after transcription on every plan", reports SOC 2 Type II certification since July 2025, and offers an MCP server on every plan, so notes can feed other tools and agents. A third-party tracker records a $125 million Series C at a $1.5 billion valuation in March 2026.

**Watch out for:** because no bot joins, the other people on the call get no visible notice. Granola's own guidance is simply to tell your team you are transcribing. You have to say it, every time. On the free tier, MCP covers only the last 30 days of notes and there is no API.

**Pricing:** Basic free with 30 days of history; Business $14 per user a month; Enterprise $35, adding SSO, SCIM, HIPAA-compliant workspaces and an audit API (as listed in November 2026).

**What would change its rank:** a built-in consent notice for other attendees.

**2. Fireflies.ai**

**Best for:** teams that want summaries and action items pushed into a CRM.

**Why it ranks here:** broad integrations, annual independent SOC 2 Type II audits, and a clear statement that "Fireflies does not use your meeting data to train AI models", with its AI vendors contractually barred from doing so. Admins can manage retention, and Enterprise adds organisation-wide retention rules and a HIPAA option with private storage.

**Watch out for:** the free tier's shared pool of AI credits covers only a handful of summaries, and the meeting bot is visible, which is good for consent and sometimes awkward with external guests.

**Pricing:** Free; Pro $10 per user a month billed annually ($18 monthly); Business $19 ($29 monthly); Enterprise $39 billed annually (third-party summary of Fireflies' pricing, July 2026; we could not open Fireflies' own pricing page this month).

**What would change its rank:** stronger decision extraction, not just action items.

**3. Fathom**

**Best for:** teams that want the most useful free tier.

**Why it ranks here:** generous free use, with a choice of bot or bot-free capture on the free plan. Bot-free recording is marked beta and was reported to be Mac-only in 2026.

**Watch out for:** AI action items start on Premium, CRM field sync and deal views need Business, and SSO moved to Enterprise in July 2026. We could not verify Fathom's security certification against a report this month.

**Pricing:** Free; Premium $16 a month billed annually ($20 monthly); Team $15 per seat annually, two-seat minimum; Business $25 annually; Enterprise by quote (per a third-party tracker's snapshot of Fathom's pricing page, July 2026, checked October 2026).

**What would change its rank:** a SOC 2 report we can review.

**4. Circleback**

**Best for:** technical teams that want to wire meeting outputs into their own systems.

**Why it ranks here:** API, MCP and command-line access are included from the free plan, with automations into Notion, HubSpot, Salesforce, Attio and webhooks on Pro, and a bot-free desktop app as an option. Business adds custom data retention, which matters if your policy says how long recordings may be kept.

**Watch out for:** a small team behind it, and its pricing page does not state a security certification; check its security site before you connect it to client calls.

**Pricing:** Free with 30 days of history; Pro $15 per user; Business $25 with custom retention; Enterprise $35 with SSO, SCIM and HIPAA (as listed in November 2026).

**What would change its rank:** evidence of scale.

**5. Google Meet with Gemini notes**

**Best for:** teams that live in Google Workspace.

**Why it ranks here:** "Take notes for me" is included in Business Standard and Business Plus, and the notes land in Google Docs that you already own and can export, with no extra vendor or data processor.

**Watch out for:** it works on Meet calls only, and not on Business Starter.

**Pricing:** included in Business Standard at $14 per user a month on an annual plan ($16.80 flexible) and Business Plus at $22 ($26.40 flexible), as listed in November 2026.

**What would change its rank:** support for calls on other platforms.

## Side by side

|  | Granola | Fireflies.ai | Fathom | Circleback | Google Meet with Gemini |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Capture | Device audio, no bot | Meeting bot | Bot, or bot-free beta | Bot, or bot-free desktop app | Inside Meet |
| How notes are made | You jot, AI enhances, you edit | AI summary and action items | AI summary; action items on Premium | AI notes and custom insights | AI notes in Docs |
| Export and agent access | MCP on all plans; API on Business | CRM integrations | Integrations; CRM sync on Business | API, MCP and CLI from free | Google Docs |
| Training on your data | Audio deleted after transcription | Stated: no | Not verified | Not verified | Workspace terms |
| Security stated | SOC 2 Type II | SOC 2 Type II, audited annually | Not verified | Not stated on pricing page | Workspace controls |
| Entry paid price, November 2026 | $14 per user a month | $10 annual | $16 annual | $15 | Business Standard, $14 annual |

> The notetaker will catch the decision only if someone says it out loud. Say the decision, the reason and what would change your mind before the call ends.

## Left out, and why

**Otter.ai.** Large and capable, but a proposed class action filed in the US District Court for the Northern District of California in August 2025 alleges that its notetaker can join meetings without the consent of any participant when calendars are linked, and that recordings are used to train its AI without permission. Otter's privacy policy says it gets explicit permission for training and de-identifies audio first. Wait for the case to resolve before recommending it for decision records.

**Read.ai.** Its meeting "engagement scoring" can put attendees off, and enterprise security features sit on its top tier.

**tl;dv.** We could not confirm current prices on its own site.

**Zoom AI Companion and Teams Copilot recap.** Good if you are already on those platforms, but tied to one meeting tool.

## How to use any of them for decisions

1. **Say at the start of the call that it is being recorded, and why.** With a bot-free tool, this is the only notice anyone gets.
2. **Before the call ends, say the decision and the reason out loud.** Add who owns it and what would make you revisit it. The notetaker will catch it.
3. **Copy the decision, reason and "what would change our mind" into your decision record the same day.** Our list of [tools for a founders' decision ledger](https://lowob.com/research/top-5-tools-for-a-founders-decision-ledger/) covers where to keep it, and our piece on [the founders' ledger](https://lowob.com/research/two-people-the-founders-ledger/) covers the habit.
4. **Set a retention period for recordings** that matches your policy, and delete the audio once the record exists.

## lowob takeaways

- **Granola ranks first for draft-and-correct notes.** Audio deleted after transcription, MCP on every plan, but no notice to other attendees.
- **Consent is a legal question.** All-party consent states such as California make an unannounced recording the host's problem.
- **Ownership means export.** Prefer tools with an API, MCP or notes in documents you already hold.
- **The record beats the transcript.** Say the decision and reason aloud, then write them down that day.

Gateway card

### Buyer's checklist for a decision-capture notetaker

- Every attendee is told the call is recorded, and why, by the tool or by you
- The vendor states in writing whether it trains on your meetings
- Notes export through an API, MCP or documents you already own
- Recordings have a retention period you can set
- A security report you can read, not only a badge
- The first paid tier includes the features you will actually use

## Common questions

### What is the best AI notetaker for capturing decisions?

This list ranks Granola first for bot-free, draft-and-correct notes that you edit, followed by Fireflies.ai, Fathom, Circleback and Google Meet with Gemini notes.

### Is it legal to use an AI notetaker without telling people?

Not everywhere. California and several other US states require the consent of all parties to record a confidential conversation, and California fines start at up to $2,500 per violation. Tell everyone on the call. This is not legal advice.

### How much do AI notetakers cost?

As listed in November 2026, Granola Business is $14 per user a month, Circleback Pro $15, Fathom Premium $16 billed annually, Fireflies Pro $10 billed annually, and Gemini notes come with Google Workspace Business Standard at $14.

### How do I use an AI notetaker to record decisions?

Announce the recording and why at the start, state the decision and reason aloud before the call ends, and copy the decision, reason and what would change your mind into a decision record the same day.
